card.name: Supreme Court and auxiliary verbs before rulings
card.fires_on: Words right before a verb of a decision or outcome, such as 'Supreme Court' (on Court or States), or a helper like 'has' or 'had' after a subject. Mostly in legal news and in 'response has not occurred' wording.

modes.label: Supreme Court naming
modes.description: Fires on Court or States inside 'Supreme Court (of the United States)', where a ruling verb comes next.
modes.example: on June 26 the Supreme<< Court>> of the United States agreed to take both

modes.label: Helper verb after a subject
modes.description: Fires on has or had after a subject noun, before a past participle describing an outcome.
modes.example: some observers suggested that the long-term decline<< had>> ended.

modes.label: Court hearing a case
modes.description: Fires on a pronoun or adverb before a court verb such as hear or visit.
modes.example: on Wednesday, when<< they>> will hear a challenge

card.writes: It pushes words like favored, validated, approved and backed, which are verbs of endorsement, and pushes down won and attracted.
card.plain: It fires where a sentence is about to say what a court or process decided or endorsed.
